records.text:
Thank you for getting back to me, sir!
Yes, the monitor dims in all modes, no matter what. Also, this is tailored to my PS5 Pro at the moment; I do not have a computer to make adjustments on that end. records.author: Hassen_Lenovo
records.text:
Hello Nate23__,
Sorry you're experiencing this issue with your monitor.
Does the dimming occur with every game and content type on the PS5, or have you only noticed it with specific games after longer play sessions?
Since you've already performed factory resets, disabled HDR, Dolby Vision, OLED care options, and recalibrated HDR, try the following:
Test the monitor with another device such as a PC, laptop, or different console for an extended period to see whether the same dimming behavior occurs.
If available, switch to a different video input on the monitor and retest.
Try a different HDMI cable to rule out a signal-related issue.
For testing purposes, temporarily disable VRR and 120 Hz output on the PS5 and check whether the behavior changes at 60 Hz.
Leave the monitor at its default picture settings during testing and avoid enabling additional image enhancement features.
Observe whether the dimming appears across multiple games or only under specific conditions.
If the monitor behaves normally with other devices, that would help narrow the focus to the video signal configuration being used with the PS5. If the dimming also occurs with different devices, inputs, and cables, please let us know the results of those tests so we can continue troubleshooting with you.
Best regards,
Hassen_Lenovo

records.author: Nate23__
records.text: First off, it’s a great monitor! The only bad experience I’m having is when the screen dims after 30–40 minutes of gameplay! The only way to disable it is to turn the monitor off manually and then back on again. I tried everything: multiple factory resets, turning HDR off, disabling OLED Care settings, disabling Dolby Vision, and recalibrating the HDR on my PS5 Pro, but it’s still the same issue with no solution! I checked online and noticed others are experiencing the same thing. Maybe I just received a faulty device—Firmware 03, 27 inch. Any other tips? I do have a 3-year warranty for this unit since I ordered directly from Lenovo’s site. If I receive a replacement, wouldn’t it just be the same??

I have since returned the monitor and bought a model from a competitor. If Lenovo cannot manage to provide an appropriate firmware update, then I will simply go to the competition. Nevertheless, thank you for your input, and I hope that this monitor continues to be usable for you.

records.source_title: HDR Dimming Issue on Lenovo Legion Pro, Can't Update Firmware 27Q-10
records.author: guest60967
records.text:
Good day,
Just bought this monitor and it has the same behaviour:
On TB400 it dimms after 30 to 60 mins. of playing and the only solution is turning it off an on, or cycling through other HDR modes, or turning off and on the HDR in Windows 11. On SDR I haven't noticed any weird dimming yet, but I read that some users have the problem even on SDR. Very unfortunate. The firmware is 04. I'm really thinking of returning the product and stay away from Lenovo related monitors, given the fact that this problem is around for a long time and no action was taken.
